segments: Bishop, what is the day of atonement?
When you read Leviticus the 23rd
chapter, the day of atonement is a day
when you fast and afflict your souls for
your sin. No eating, no drinking. In
conjunction with that, when you read
Isaiah 58, and bear with me a second in
verse 6, it says, "Is not this the fast
that I have chosen to loose the bands of
wickedness, to undo the heavy burdens,
and to let the oppressed go free, that
you break every yoke." So on the day of
atonement, we have to go out, teach the
people to break those the the spirit of
oppression that is on our people. That's
what the teaching does. He don't, the
Most High, when you read Isaiah 58, he
doesn't want us just sitting home, you
know, with a disfigured face, your
hair's all jacked up. He want us anoint
our head with oil like it says in
Matthew. Then he says to go out and
teach the word to help the people. So
that's what the David at Tone is
